html:
I took a quick look at the options for powering the telescope. Power supply units are offered by telescope companies like Celestron and by companies like Canadian Tire.

My immediate need was mostly for the LX90. Since the 8 C batteries it takes cost about $10, the savings from a rechargeable battery are substantial and grow the more I use the telescope. Also, I don't plan on using heater bands or other accessories for now. In my experience, a dew shield is quite effective for observing sessions of 3-4 hours.

I settled on Celestron's PowerTank . It has a 7 amp-hour battery, which should be enough to run the LX90 for 4-5 hours. Plus it's not too big.

When I need more current (heater bands, computer, etc.), I'll add a bigger battery.

I'll talk about the PowerTank again once I've been out a few times, especially about the battery life.
